Singapore's position as a leading financial and innovation hub makes it an important part of this global strategy. In Singapore, the planned custody service will complement the Bank's broader Financing & Securities Services capabilities, bringing together traditional asset servicing, tokenisation and digital asset custody. This marks a significant milestone as we prepare to bring our digital asset custody capabilities to clients in Singapore. It also reinforces our commitment to supporting the development of a secure and well-regulated digital asset ecosystem in the market." Sharing a Group perspective, Ole Matthiessen, Global Head, Transaction Services & Digital Assets, Standard Chartered, said: "Secure and regulated custody is a critical foundation of the digital asset ecosystem. As a GSIB we provide the trust, security and institutional safeguards needed to support broader market participation and adoption, and we are pleased to bring this capability to Singapore. highlights: Bitget Cross-Asset Account cuts USDT margin by $165,000 on a $1M portfolio | BitInsider Bitget Cross-Asset Account cuts USDT margin by $165,000 on a $1M portfolio Bitget’s push to let traders use almost any asset as collateral at once is now being tested against a simple question: does more flexibility actually free up capital, or does it just move the risk somewhere else? Collateral that moves with a trader’s positions can push liquidation up to six percentage points closer than holding USDT. Bitget’s wider Universal Exchange gives traders access to over 2 million cryptocurrencies plus a growing set of tokenised real-world assets. The analysis comes from Block Scholes, which was commissioned by Bitget to examine the product but says it kept full editorial independence over its data, methodology and conclusions. The report centers on what it calls the next competitive frontier in crypto trading: not just offering access to many asset types, but making that access capital-efficient . Bitget Launches Cross-Asset Unified Account for Capital-Efficient Trading Bitget’s Cross-Asset Unified Account , or UTA, launched in July 2026 as the next stage of its Universal Exchange (UEX) product, built to serve the exchange’s user base of more than 125 million people worldwide. Product launch details and asset support The account supports more than 370 eligible assets as margin, among them 125 tokenised US stocks, alongside crypto-native perpetual swaps. Instead of sitting idle in separate, siloed balances, these holdings can now back open positions directly, pooling collateral across asset classes rather than locking it away per account. Capital efficiency gains quantified Block Scholes measured the effect on a representative $1 million portfolio combining tokenised equities with crypto-native perpetual swaps. Running that portfolio through UTA required roughly $165,000 less USDT margin than a traditional siloed setup, cutting capital needs by close to half and bringing the margin requirement down to about 16.5% of notional. Collateral Correlation and Liquidation Risk in Multi-Asset Portfolios Freeing up margin comes with a tradeoff tied to how closely a trader’s collateral tracks the positions it backs. The efficiency gain from multi-asset capital efficiency depends heavily on the type of collateral used, not just its amount. Impact of collateral type and correlation on liquidation When collateral moves in the same direction as the portfolio it supports, both can fall together during a market-wide sell-off, pulling the account toward liquidation faster. In the multi-asset equity and crypto portfolio Block Scholes examined, that correlation effect brought the liquidation point six percentage points closer than if the trader had held the same collateral in USDT instead. Tradeoffs and risk mitigation with stablecoins Block Scholes frames this as a choice traders make. Holding less-correlated assets or stablecoin collateral can offset the collateral correlation risk that comes with using tokenised stocks or crypto tokens as margin for related positions. text: ### Finding

The claim is **supported**. Digital asset research firm Block Scholes and cryptocurrency exchange Bitget published a research report titled *"Capital Efficiency, Correlation Risk and Multi-Asset Trading on Bitget’s Cross-Asset Unified Account"*, which modeled a representative $1 million multi-asset portfolio and found that using tokenized equities as shared collateral reduced required committed capital by approximately $165,000 (from ~$340,000 to ~$175,000).
### Evidence

* **Modeled Portfolio Specifications:** Block Scholes simulated a $1,000,000 multi-asset portfolio holding $175,000 in tokenized U.S. equities (specifically AI and semiconductor stocks), long BTC and ETH perpetual swap positions, and a short Nasdaq-100 ETF perpetual position.

* **Capital Reduction Mechanics:** In a conventional siloed trading structure, the portfolio required roughly $340,000 in dedicated capital ($175,000 in stock holdings plus ~$165,000 in separate USDT margin). Under Bitget’s Cross-Asset Unified Account (UTA)—which allows 370+ assets, including 125 tokenized U.S. stocks, to serve as shared margin—the stock holdings themselves back the derivative positions, lowering total required committed capital to ~$175,000 (a reduction of ~$165,000, or roughly half).

* **Collateral Correlation Risk:** The report noted that this capital efficiency introduces heightened liquidation risk when collateral is correlated with open positions. Under stress testing, a portfolio backed by tokenized equity collateral reached liquidation after a ~21% correlated market decline, compared to a ~27% decline when backed by USDT—bringing liquidation 6 percentage points closer.
### Context

* **Bitget’s Universal Exchange (UEX) Model:** Bitget introduced cross-asset margining to integrate traditional financial assets (tokenized stocks, ETFs, commodities) with crypto spot and derivatives markets. This allows single-position utility where an asset can simultaneously maintain underlying exposure (and receive USDT dividends) while acting as margin or borrowing collateral.

* **Institutional Context:** Block Scholes conducted the quantitative modeling. While commissioned by Bitget to evaluate the Cross-Asset Unified Account, Block Scholes stated it retained editorial and methodological independence.
### Uncertainty & Limitations

* **Model vs. Live Trading:** The $165,000 capital savings figure is derived from a specific, static theoretical portfolio model ($1M portfolio with a specific mix of equities and crypto perpetuals). Actual savings vary significantly based on portfolio composition, asset volatility, haircuts, and leverage levels.

* **Risk Caveat:** The headline emphasizes capital efficiency benefits, but the primary conclusion of the Block Scholes report is a risk-return trade-off: capital efficiency gains directly increase vulnerability to correlated sell-offs.

highlights: Writer and director Mackenzie Crook explores grief and whimsy in Small Prophets, a series about a man attempting to grow Biblical homunculi to solve the mystery of his missing girlfriend. Yet that is precisely what has happened. As Gervais burns up all the goodwill he acquired playing Brent with his tragic live shows and dire Netflix comedies, Crook has quietly created a new genre where wry laughter and heartbreaking whimsy live together in uneasy coexistence. That was the formula he unlocked on Detectorists, with its droll profile of male friendships, and his funny/spooky revival of Worzel Gummidge . He now ascends to a Pokémon-style final evolutionary stage with the wonderful magical realist chuckle-fest Small Prophets, which comes to Apple TV eight months after it debuted on the BBC . In theory, the story of depressed middle-aged DIY store worker Michael and his quest to grow Biblical homunculi in his shed really should not work at all. But Crook, directs all six , invests such humanity in his portrait of a man his maudlin existence that it is Crook himself plays Michael’s David Brent-esque boss, while Lauren Patel shines i plot. But their thunder is thoroughly stolen by Michael Palin Michael’s has been bunged off to care home and is in the early of dementia. It is during one of his increasingly rare moments of clarity that he beseeches Michael to cultivate the homunculi – Brian picked up the know-how in Egypt – so that they can solve the mystery around the whereabouts of Michael’s girlfriend, who vanished without a trace seven years previously, condemning Michael to a state of permanent stasis. The magical realism of Small Prophets places it firmly in the firmament of urbane British fantasy and figures such as Terry Pratchett – but this isn’t what all viewers will have signed up for, and to some it is going to be a deal-breaker. It’s like turning on Alan Partridge only for someone to ride in on the back of a dragon. They would do well to persevere however as these elements only serve to accentuate the sad plod of Michael’s daily life and to raise the dramatic stakes of his quietly affectionate exchanges with his ailing dad. Mashing together the bizarre and the banal, Small Prophets is funny, fantastical and, above all, heartbreakingly tender.
